reply_text:
㊥ (M-x turn-stepper) `M-x turn-stepper` works again. It's loaded in your running Emacs now, and `futon0/contrib/futon-config.el` requires it right after `session-mode`, so it will load after a restart too. Committed as `4b173b1` in futon0 and pushed.

㊢ (what changed) Two lines:
- `(require 'turn-stepper)`, next to the other `session-mode` requires;
- `turn-stepper.el` added to the hot-reload list, so edits to it reload the way `session-mode.el` does.

The parenthesis check passes. I also checked that the stepper's "reading landed" hook is registered again, so an open stepper refreshes on its own when a reading lands.

㊟ (other files not loaded) `futon-config.el` doesn't load two other 象 files either:
- **`xiang-trace.el`:** the trace checker that adds a "!rule ×N" segment to the 象 lighter.
- **`xiaoxiang-preview.el`:** the 小象 preview hydra.

They were presumably loaded by hand before, so they were also lost in the crash. Shall I add them the same way? I've left them out for now, since you only asked for the stepper.

🈳 (still open) After the restart the recorder is back to `files`, so your turns aren't using the fast path. `(setq session-mode-turn-recorder 'jvm)` turns it back on. I can also make `jvm` the saved default in `futon-config.el`, once we've timed a few turns on it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (*Warnings* popping up) The warnings popping up now aren't from the 象 recorder. Both of your last turns were recorded through the JVM cleanly (`turn-elJzmq` is analysed; this one, `turn-PhLBYe`, is waiting for my reply to end). The three "NOT recorded" lines are left over from before the parser fix. The new warnings come from `server-dead-client.el`: "20 emacsclient replies dropped in the last 5 min". It warns when Emacs answers emacsclient calls too slowly and the callers give up.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what that warning means) Agency runs emacsclient calls against your Emacs, for example the blackboard projections, and kills them if they're slow. The file's own note says the cause on 2026-10-03 was "six forgotten tty frames redrawing busy REPL buffers". The counter is at 1,183 drops in total, with 5 in the current 5-minute window, so it's quieter at the moment. It warns at most once every 10 minutes.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (not the recorder) I timed the JVM turn route at about 1 ms per request. Recording at send is synchronous, but it doesn't stall Emacs. The polls for readings are asynchronous.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(frames) Your Emacs has four tty frames besides the initial one:
- **F16** on `/dev/pts/2`: this buffer
- **F13** on `/dev/pts/24`: `*codex-repl:codex-19*`
- **F12** on `/dev/pts/21`: `*codex-repl:codex-10*`
- **F14** on `/dev/pts/21`: a corfu completion popup

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (one decision) Is F12 (codex-10, on pts/21) a frame you still use? If not, closing it with `C-x 5 0` in that terminal should cut the redraw load. I can delete it from here if you prefer. Separately, I could make the warning log to `*Messages*` instead of popping up `*Warnings*`, if you'd rather it didn't interrupt.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (slicing the inference) On the different ways to slice the inference: rather than picking one now, 象 could produce more than one reading of the same pair, and we see which ones prove useful. That fits the M-象-cascade view that multiplicity "is information too". I'll put it in the lab note if you want that written.
